category_title: Students experiencing sensory overload and avoidance behaviors due to trauma
minimal_context: Natasha is reviewing a returned logic-based paper in front of her English class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Natasha, here is your returned paper. You missed the point on the logic section of this assignment, so please review the corrections.

STUDENT: (Starts doodling and drawing on the paper) I have zero concentration right now. It is hard to do something like school that's logic when you don't have any logic left.

TUTOR: Please stop drawing and look at the feedback. We are going over this in front of the class so everyone can see where they went wrong.

STUDENT: (Looking jittery and restless) I can't do this right now. Something as simple as being in class is just too hard.

TUTOR: You need to focus on the academic task. Look at the paper and try to figure out the logic.

STUDENT: (Stands up, looking overwhelmed and on the verge of tears) I need to physically dismiss myself. I'm going to the girls' bathroom.

options.A: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing and returning the assignments in the class.
options.B: Require three revisions per assignment and only grade the final submitted draft for the class.
options.C: Begin grading the student with more rigor, expecting work of a superior quality on the assignments.
options.D: Notice the student, validate their distress, reach out to them, and look out for their overall well-being.
